info.title: Xynolog Archivist
info.description:
The Archivist's HTTP surface: what the gateway (and only the fleet's own services) call to store and read the knowledge base's bytes, read its linked-data descriptions and the text extracted from its content, and read the event log by position, to replay a resource's events and to follow the record; and what the Smelter calls to keep the anchored-text store. Everything else reaches the Archivist over the bus.

**How long a caller waits.** A caller gives the Archivist `x-xynolog-limits.connectSeconds` to take its connection, and `readSeconds` for each part of an answer: for the answer to begin once its request is sent whole, and for each next part of an answer that streams. Past either, the call has failed. A connection not taken within `connectSeconds` means the Archivist cannot be reached: that call is not made again. No bound is put on a whole answer, nor on sending a request: a large upload or a large document takes as long as it takes, as long as it keeps coming.

The waits nest, so the one inside ends first and is answered: `readSeconds` is longer than the Archivist holds a read of anchored text for the Smelter (`settleWaitSeconds` of `GET /resources/{id}/anchored-text`), and `connectSeconds` and `readSeconds` together, within which the answer to a read the gateway makes begins from the read's first send, its retry included, are shorter than a client's deadline on a request to the gateway (`httpRequestTimeoutMs`, specs/src/client/timing.json), so a read the gateway makes for a client has failed, and the gateway has answered, before the client stops waiting. The reader's protocol rules (`reader/lib/protocol_rules.ml`) hold the order.

servers.description: The address the gateway's configuration names (`archivist.host`, `archivist.port`).

serviceAccount.description: `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` from the knowledge base's trusted issuer — the issuer and audience the `bearerAuth` scheme of the gateway's API names — carrying `xynolog-service` in its flat `roles` claim: a service account of this knowledge base. People never call the Archivist; the gateway does, as itself, and so do the stack's own services: the Smelter keeps the anchored-text store here.
